The `boot` package [@davison1997bootstrap],
a recommended package distributed with R,
provides `boot::boot()` to draw the bootstrap replicates
and `boot::boot.ci()` to compute the three intervals.
`boot::boot.ci()` differs from the definitions on this page
in two small ways:

- its normal interval (`type = "norm"`) is centered at
  $\hat\theta$ minus the bootstrap estimate of bias,
  $\hat\theta - (\bar\theta^* - \hat\theta)$,
  where $\bar\theta^*$ is the mean of the replicates,
  rather than at $\hat\theta$;
- it estimates quantiles of the replicates by interpolation,
  so its percentile and BCa endpoints can differ slightly
  from those computed with `quantile()`.
